answer: Random re-execution, nothing clever. Peers drawn from a rotating pool re-run one job in ten, and a mismatch voids the submission along with the bond behind it. Auditors cannot be chosen, so buying them means buying the pool. Duplicates fall out of payload hashes, which is the shale under every rename. A ten thousand account farm is one sonnet with a single line, and the falcon of a spot check reads it in one pass. Cost, one duplicated job in ten, paid forever.
